decisions.reason: F2 attributed the derivative-coefficient formula to a Parseval statement that contains only Fourier isometry/completeness. New step 1.2 derives it by smooth periodic integration by parts; Parseval then gives both norm sums and the sharp constant one. The original Statement is unchanged.

For W nonzero the displayed solution contains a stationary transverse zero mode in addition to the longitudinal acoustic pair. Corrected the title to say so, retaining all A,B,W cases. Direct amplitude differentiation and normalized sine/cosine integrals verify the complete solution and conserved weighted energy.

The old step 1.1 proved only finite bounds for each fixed viscosity, not the stated uniform family bound. The repaired step derives the Hm transport energy inequality using the exact tame-commutator supplier, discards nonpositive viscous dissipation, and integrates Hs and higher-order inequalities on a common viscosity-independent interval. All difference and interpolation estimates remain valid; Statement unchanged.

The original proof used quantitative restart and r-change estimates absent from the public IVP statements. Replaced this dependency-citation gap with a local endpoint argument: tame high-order energy bounds, time-Lipschitz convergence in every complete Hm, positive smooth endpoint density, local existence from endpoint data, and matching all time derivatives across the join. No quantitative restart formula is assumed; both original claims are retained.

F1 included a specific lifespan formula absent from the cited local theorem statement, but no proof step uses it. Removed that nonfatal overstatement. Checked enstrophy time integration, Fourier-log commutator control, regularized logarithmic differentiation, and the finite-H4 continuation contradiction; all original global and quantitative conclusions remain unchanged.
